correctness.rationale: The two phase matrices square to ab I. Their exponentials have determinant one after factoring recovery and trace 2[1+2 Gamma^2 sinh^2 z], so the exact Perron multiplier and exponent follow. The second derivative of asinh(Gamma sinh z) is strictly negative for all z>0, Gamma>1; secant slopes are strictly decreasing. Correct limiting values, unique crossing, endpoint equalities, and Taylor expansions follow. Direct matrix-exponential tests 300 random parameter cases and 250 derivative comparisons passed; numerical evidence is subordinate to the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The qualitative converse epidemic switching effect is covered by Ait Rami et al. 2013/2014 and expressly excluded from the new claim. The asserted original quantitative contribution is the closed continuous-time reciprocal-directed exponent, its strict all-period monotonicity and necessary/sufficient unique period boundary with square-root onset. The source 2024 treatment restricts numerical tests to symmetric networks and neither it nor the inspected 2013/2015 general results states these exact relationships. Analogous two-patch dispersal histories have different structural assumptions and the opposite curvature. value.rationale: The 2024 temporal-network SIS paper reports no opposite paradox among its symmetric examples; 2013 literature guarantees only that some sufficiently fast switching can create persistence when the average contact layer is unstable. The new exact two-group reciprocal-directed family provides an entire period-resolved stability classification, sharp recovery window, unique quantitative cutoff and square-root onset. Those answers distinguish directed contact asymmetry and frequency choice in a natural contagion setting; not a renamed stability check or a generic existence corollary.
